```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE, cache = FALSE)
library(llmsa)
documentation <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("validation", "m1d", "findings.R", package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE),
           envir = documentation)
anchors <- documentation$m1d_resources()
source_contract <- anchors[["ANK-40"]]$value
read_items <- function(path) {
  con <- gzfile(path, "rt")
  on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE)
  utils::read.csv(con, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "", encoding = "UTF-8")
}
items <- read_items(system.file("extdata", "llm-stability_2026-10-22", "items.csv.gz",
                               package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE))
provenance <- readLines(system.file("extdata", "llm-stability_2026-10-22", "QUELLE.txt",
                                   package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE), encoding = "UTF-8")
```

The frozen public data from [Atil et al.'s llm-stability repository](https://github.com/breckbaldwin/llm-stability)
contain **`r nrow(items)` calls** across **`r length(source_contract$models)` models**,
**`r length(source_contract$tasks)` tasks** and **`r source_contract$n_runs` runs**.
ANK-40 fixes commit **`r source_contract$commit`**, the Apache 2.0 licence and
the complete v3 zero-shot selection. The model configuration uses temperature
`r source_contract$model_config$temperature` and top_p_k
`r source_contract$model_config$top_p_k`. These are recorded historical calls;
building this article makes no model calls and needs no external data.

The preparation script `data-raw/make_llm_stability.R` verifies the source
hashes and the complete item grid before publishing the subset. `SHA256SUMS`
covers the stored gzip file and its provenance. The archive contains other
configurations, which are outside this selection.

## What counts as an answer

The parser accepts exactly one distinct valid option label such as `(A)`
in parentheses, ignoring letter case, with no spaces inside the parentheses.
Bare letters, including the English words "A" and "I", do not count.
Repeated occurrences of the same label count once; different labels anywhere
in the response, including quoted alternatives, make the answer ambiguous.
There is no priority for a final sentence. For `navigate`, exactly one of
the whole words "Yes" or "No" is required. The key never selects an answer.
An empty, unparseable or ambiguous response remains missing.

`correct` compares the parsed label literally with the source key. A missing
answer has missing correctness. The source also contains non-label keys:

```{r key-format-note, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat(grep("^Non-label answer keys:", provenance, value = TRUE), "\n\n")
```

For these `ruin_names` items, every parsed option label counts as a miss under
literal label/key equality, even when its meaning matches the intended answer.
The data retain that limitation; the keys are not repaired. Thus the hit rate
describes this extraction rule, not a human reassessment of the response text.
The provenance records parsing failures by reason, task and model. Raw response
texts are not distributed.

## Observed repeatability and hit rate

For each task and model, attribute repeatability is the fraction of items
with a present, identical answer in every run. A missing answer breaks
agreement. The hit rate divides the number of `correct == TRUE` calls by
**all** calls, including missing answers. The missing-answer share is shown
alongside both quantities. None of these denominators depends on a fit.

```{r observed-rates}
cells <- split(items, list(items$task, items$model), drop = TRUE)
rates <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cells, function(d) {
  answers <- split(d$answer, d$item_id)
  identical_answers <- vapply(answers, function(x) !anyNA(x) && length(unique(x)) == 1L, logical(1))
  data.frame(task = d$task[1L], model = d$model[1L], items = length(answers), calls = nrow(d),
    answer_repeatability = mean(identical_answers), hit_rate = mean(d$correct %in% TRUE),
    missing_answer_share = mean(is.na(d$answer)))
}))
rownames(rates) <- NULL
```

```{r rates-table, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
print(knitr::kable(documentation$m1d_display(rates), row.names = FALSE,
                   caption = "Observed proportions, with all items or calls in the denominator."))
```

## Binary variance components

Each task gets its own binary fit. Item is the question, model is the source
model, and replicate is the original run number. The one prompt and one block
level are constant. `msa_counts()` counts all imported calls, including those
whose correctness is missing. The fit drops those missing responses, with its
warning recorded below; it does not recode them as false. Fits use the default
probit link and no interactions. Each fit and `msa_grr()` is recomputed here.

```{r binary-fits}
analyses <- lapply(unique(items$task), function(task) {
  d <- items[items$task == task, , drop = FALSE]
  runs <- as_msa_runs(data.frame(item_id = as.character(d$item_id), prompt_id = "task",
                                 model_id = d$model, rep = d$run, value = as.integer(d$correct)))
  counts <- msa_counts(runs)
  diagnostics <- character()
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(msa_fit(runs, type = "binary", interactions = FALSE, link = "probit"),
    warning = function(w) {
      diagnostics <<- c(diagnostics, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }, message = function(m) {
      diagnostics <<- c(diagnostics, conditionMessage(m)); invokeRestart("muffleMessage")
    })
  grr <- msa_grr(fit)
  components <- setNames(fit$vc$variance, fit$vc$source)
  list(counts = data.frame(task = task, counts),
    summary = data.frame(task = task, item = components[["item"]], model = components[["model"]],
      grr_pct_study_var = grr$summary[["grr_pct_study_var"]], observations = fit$n$observations,
      converged = fit$converged, singular = fit$singular),
    diagnostics = data.frame(task = task, diagnostic = if (length(diagnostics)) paste(unique(diagnostics), collapse = " | ") else "none"))
})
```

```{r binary-tables, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
print(knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(analyses, `[[`, "counts")), row.names = FALSE,
                   caption = "Imported counts from msa_counts(); missing responses are included."))
cat("\n\n")
print(knitr::kable(documentation$m1d_display(do.call(rbind, lapply(analyses, `[[`, "summary"))),
                   row.names = FALSE, caption = "Latent variance components and percent GRR study variation."))
cat("\n\n")
print(knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(analyses, `[[`, "diagnostics")), row.names = FALSE,
                   caption = "Recorded fit warnings and messages."))
```

The latent residual variance is fixed by the link. It is not a measurement
of observed disagreement between repeated calls; use the answer-repeatability
table for that question. Large latent item components can accompany a flat
likelihood, and missing responses can select which calls enter the model.
The convergence and singularity flags describe the actual fit. AIAG bands
on this scale are conventions, not evidence of correctness or suitability
for another use. See `vignette("validation")` for engine comparisons and
the simulation findings, including bias with few prompt or model levels.
